DAMGHANI:v1p289/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p289/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p289/r8.claim: Ḍaʿīf can describe someone who cannot restrain his desire for women.
DAMGHANI:v1p289/r8.anchor: الضعيف من لا صبر له عن التزويج قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p603#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p603#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p603#2/r4.claim: The unstated object of “God wants to lighten for you” has several proposed senses: concessions such as slave marriage, clarified rules, removal of earlier burdens, reward for obligations, or pardon for ignorant sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p603#2/r4.anchor: يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم لم يذكر متعلق التخفيف، وفي ذلك أقوال:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p603#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p603#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p603#2/r5.claim: Treating the clause as circumstantial from “God wants to grant you repentance” is grammatically weak because a separate coordinated clause intervenes and the verb takes an explicit subject; the author prefers an independent sentence, like the promise of ease.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p603#2/r5.anchor: وأعربوا هذه الجملة حالا من قوله: والله يريد أن يتوب عليكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p603#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p603#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p603#2/r6.claim: The author prefers taking “God wants to lighten for you” as an independent sentence with no syntactic role, parallel to God's statement that He wants ease for people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p603#2/r6.anchor: والأحسن أن تكون الجملة مستأنفة، فلا موضع لها من الإعراب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p605/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p605/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p605/r5.claim: Expressions imply linked rules: reluctance hints consensual inheritance transfer; the ban on coercing wives allows restraint for their benefit; the prohibition on fathers' wives recalls pre-Islamic practice; permission points to prior bans; slave-marriage conditions and human weakness point to desire.

TABATABAI:4:23-28#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:23-28#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:23-28#5/r1.claim: The stated aim of easing religious burdens connects with the prayer against burdens imposed on earlier communities and the declaration that religion contains no hardship; it displays the fullness of God's human blessings in this community.
TABATABAI:4:23-28#5/r1.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن النكتة في هذا التعليل العام بيان ظهور تمام النعم الإنسانية في هذه الأمة

THALABI:v3p290/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p290/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p290/r10.claim: God intends to ease marriage to enslaved women when one cannot afford a free wife and to ease the rulings of the Law; humans are weak.
THALABI:v3p290/r10.anchor: يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم في نكاح الأمة، إذا لم تجدوا طول الجرة وفي كل أحكام الشرع وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا

THALABI:v3p290/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p290/r11.speaker: طاوس والكلبي وأكثر المفسرين
THALABI:v3p290/r11.claim: They interpret human weakness specifically as lack of restraint in sexual desire and weakness concerning women.
THALABI:v3p290/r11.anchor: طاوس والكلبي وأكثر المفسرين: يعني في أمر الجماع لا يصبر على النساء

THALABI:v3p290/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p290/r12.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
THALABI:v3p290/r12.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says Satan approaches people through women and that even at eighty he most fears their temptation.
THALABI:v3p290/r12.anchor: قال سعيد بن المسيب: ما آيس الشيطان من بني آدم إلا أتاه من قبل النساء

THALABI:v3p290/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p290/r13.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
THALABI:v3p290/r13.claim: Ubadah says he would not risk being alone with a forbidden woman, despite his wealth, because he feared Satan could exploit the situation.
THALABI:v3p290/r13.anchor: وما يسرني أني خلوت بامرأة لا تحل لي وأن لي ما تطلع عليه الشمس مخافة أن يأتيني الشيطان

STUDYQURAN:4:26/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r4.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r4.claim: God lightens the burden by allowing men without sufficient means to marry enslaved women.
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r4.anchor: allowing men of insufficient means to marry slave women—for man was created weak

STUDYQURAN:4:26/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r5.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r5.claim: Human weakness here is a generally limited capacity to resist sexual desire and attraction to women for long.
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r5.anchor: with a generally weak capacity to resist sexual desire and attraction to women for long (Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:4:26/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r6.claim: The Quran also describes God lightening the burden for Muslims in other ways.
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r6.anchor: The Quran mentions that God lightened the burden for Muslims in other ways (8:66)

STUDYQURAN:4:26/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r7.claim: Accommodations for human weakness include marital relations on Ramadan nights and a reduction of daily prayers at the Prophet’s request during the Night Journey.
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r7.anchor: similar accommodations for human weakness are implied in permitting sexual relations between spouses on the nights of Ramadan (2:187) and in God’s reducing the number of daily prayers at the Prophet’s request during the Night Journey (IK).

STUDYQURAN:4:26/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r8.claim: God’s desire for ease for servants is stated elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r8.anchor: The Quran states that God desires ease for His servants (2:185)

STUDYQURAN:4:26/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r9.claim: Muslim religious obligations are easier than those of earlier communities and obligations they imposed on themselves.
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r9.anchor: other verses indicate that the religious obligations of Muslims are easier than those of earlier communities (7:157) and those they impose on themselves (3:93).

STUDYQURAN:4:26/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r10.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās counts verses 26–28 among eight verses in the sūrah demonstrating God’s mercy toward humanity, alongside verses 31, 40, 48, 110, and 147.
STUDYQURAN:4:26/r10.anchor: Ibn ʿAbbās considered vv. 26–28 to be among the eight important verses in this sūrah that demonstrate God’s Mercy toward human beings (the others are vv. 31, 40, 48, 110, 147; R, Z).

TAB-FULL:v6p624/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p624/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p624/r1.claim: God makes matters easier by permitting a man unable to afford a free woman to marry a believing bondwoman when he fears sexual sin.

TAB-FULL:v6p624/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p624/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p624/r2.claim: Human beings are weak because they have little patience for abstaining from intercourse; the permission prevents fornication when they cannot afford a free woman.
TAB-FULL:v6p624/r2.anchor: لأنكم خلقتم ضعفاء عجزة عن ترك جماع النساء قليلي الصبر عنه، فأذن لكم في نكاح فتياتكم المؤمنات،

TAB-FULL:v6p624/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p624/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v6p624/r3.claim: Mujahid says the easing concerns marriage to a bondwoman and, more generally, everything in which God grants ease.
TAB-FULL:v6p624/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: {يريد الله أن يخفف، عنكم} [النساء: 28] في نكاح الأمة، وفي كل شيء فيه يسر

TAB-FULL:v6p624/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p624/r4.speaker: طاوس
TAB-FULL:v6p624/r4.claim: Tawus interprets human weakness specifically in matters of intercourse and women.
TAB-FULL:v6p624/r4.anchor: عن ابن طاوس، عن أبيه: {وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا} [النساء: 28] قال: «في أمر الجماع»

TAB-FULL:v6p624/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p624/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v6p624/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says God permitted marriage to bondwomen in cases of need; without this concession, a man unable to find a free woman would remain under the original ruling.
TAB-FULL:v6p624/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم} [النساء: 28] قال: " رخص لكم في نكاح هؤلاء الإماء حين اضطروا إليهن

TABATABAI:4:27-28/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r3.claim: Human weakness stems from implanted sexual powers that continually contend for desired objects and urge people to pursue them.
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r3.anchor: كون الإنسان ضعيفا لما ركب الله فيه القوى الشهوية التي لا تزال تنازعه في ما تتعلق به من المشتهيات

TABATABAI:4:27-28/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r4.claim: God eases that pressure by permitting marriage and ownership of female slaves, breaking the force of desire and guiding this community along the way of earlier peoples.
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r4.anchor: فمن الله عليهم بتشريع حلية ما تنكسر به سورة شهوتهم بتجويز النكاح

TABATABAI:4:27-28/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r5.claim: He identifies an additional easing as the legislation of temporary marriage, which carries none of the burdens of ordinary marriage such as dowry and maintenance.
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r5.anchor: وزادهم تخفيفا منه لهم لتشريع نكاح المتعة إذ ليس معه كلفة النكاح وما يستتبعه من أثقال الوظائف من صداق ونفقة

TABATABAI:4:27-28/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r6.claim: An unnamed view takes the easing to mean permission to marry slave women when necessary.
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r6.anchor: وربما قيل إن المراد به إباحة نكاح الإماء عند الضرورة تخفيفا

TABATABAI:4:27-28/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī objects that this marriage already existed before Islam, though disliked; these verses remove aversion by affirming the enslaved woman's equal humanity and fitness for companionship.
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r7.anchor: والذي ابتدعته هذه الآيات هو التسبب إلى نفي هذه الكراهة والنفرة ببيان أن الأمة كالحرة إنسان لا تفاوت بينهما

TABATABAI:4:27-28/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r8.claim: The address is plainly to believers in this community, so the easing is specific to them and means the legislation of temporary marriage described above.
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r8.anchor: أن الخطاب فيها متوجه إلى المؤمنين من هذه الأمة

TABATABAI:4:27-28/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:27-28/r9.claim: Human weakness is a general cause for easing, but earlier nations were kept from its effects by impediments; when repentance reached this community, mercy spread and the cause took effect.

TABRISI:4:27-28/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:27-28/r5.speaker: مجاهد وطاوس
TABRISI:4:27-28/r5.claim: Mujāhid and Ṭāwūs say God lightens the rules concerning women and marriage by permitting marriage to enslaved women.
TABRISI:4:27-28/r5.anchor: يعني في التكليف في أمر النساء والنكاح بإباحة نكاح الإماء عن مجاهد وطاوس

TABRISI:4:27-28/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:27-28/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:27-28/r6.claim: The lightening may refer to accepting repentance and enabling people to repent.
TABRISI:4:27-28/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد التخفيف بقبول التوبة والتوفيق لها

TABRISI:4:27-28/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:27-28/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:27-28/r7.claim: Alternatively, God lightens the general burden of religious obligations, giving this community less than earlier communities bore.
TABRISI:4:27-28/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد التخفيف في التكليف على العموم وذلك أنه تعالى خفف عن هذه الأمة

TABRISI:4:27-28/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:27-28/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:27-28/r8.claim: Human weakness here concerns women: people have little patience in resisting them.
TABRISI:4:27-28/r8.anchor: في أمر النساء وقلة الصبر عنهن

TABRISI:4:27-28/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:27-28/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:27-28/r9.claim: Another view says people are weak because desire pulls them and fear and grief overwhelm them.
TABRISI:4:27-28/r9.anchor: وقيل: خلق الإنسان ضعيفا يستميله هواه وشهوته ويستشيطه خوفه وحزنه

THALABI:v3p291/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p291/r1.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v3p291/r1.claim: Al-Hasan takes human weakness to mean that humanity was created from lowly fluid, citing 30:54, which says people were created from weakness.
THALABI:v3p291/r1.anchor: قال الحسن: هو أن خلقه من ماء مهين بيانه قول الله: الذي خلقكم من ضعف

THALABI:v3p291/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p291/r2.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v3p291/r2.claim: Ibn Kaysan says a person is weak because desire and appetite draw him in, while fear and grief unsettle him.
THALABI:v3p291/r2.anchor: ابن كيسان: (خلق الإنسان ضعيفا) يستميله هواه وشهوته

THALABI:v3p291/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p291/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v3p291/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says eight verses in al-Nisaʾ are better for this community than all that the sun rises and sets upon: 4:26, 4:27, 4:28, 4:31, 4:48, 4:40, 4:110, and 4:147.
THALABI:v3p291/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ثمان آيات في سورة النساء هي خير لهذه الأمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p466/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p466/r1.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p466/r1.claim: Mujahid and Muqatil restrict God's easing to allowing marriage to a female slave in cases of necessity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p466/r1.anchor: فقال: المراد به نكاح الأمة عند الضرورة. وهو قول مجاهد (¬1) ومقاتل (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p466/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p466/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p466/r2.claim: The broader view includes all legal rulings and whatever God makes easy as a kindness, contrasting with the burdens placed on the Children of Israel; Ibn Abbas explains that God eases severe obligations.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p466/r2.anchor: وعلى العموم دل كلام ابن عباس في تفسيره هذا التخفيف فقال: يريد شدة المئونة يخففها عنكم (¬3).

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:26-29/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:26-29/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:26-29/r5.claim: God wants to lighten all religious rulings because humans are weak in resisting desire for women.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:26-29/r5.anchor: { يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم } في كل أحكام الشرع { وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا } يضعف من الصبر عن النساء.

ELMALILI:4:28/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:28/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:28/r1.claim: God wants to remove burdensome obligations and lighten people's accountability because humanity was created weak.
ELMALILI:4:28/r1.anchor: Allah teâlâ sizden ağır teklifleri kaldırıp mes’ûliyetinizi tahfif etmek ister. Zira insan zayıf olarak halk edilmiştir.

ELMALILI:4:28/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:28/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:28/r2.claim: Legislation may not permit following lust, but it may not impose excessive severity or oppression either.
ELMALILI:4:28/r2.anchor: bâb-ı teşrî‘de şehvete tâbi‘olmak câiz olmadığı gibi şiddet ü tazyik de câiz değildir.

ELMALILI:4:28/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:28/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:28/r3.claim: He treats the easing as an answer to the prayer against burdens and links it with scripture's repeated principle of ease and removal of hardship.
ELMALILI:4:28/r3.anchor: dualarının bir eser-i icâbeti vardır ki

ELMALILI:4:28/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:28/r4.speaker: Peygamber
ELMALILI:4:28/r4.claim: A Prophetic hadith says he was sent with the upright, easy, and lenient way; Elmalılı cites it as affirming relief in religion.
ELMALILI:4:28/r4.anchor: جِئْتُكُمْ بِالحَْنِيفِي َّةِ ال َّسهْلَةِ ال َّسمْحَةِ hadîs-i nebevîsi

ELMALILI:4:28/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:28/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:28/r5.claim: People cannot bear severity and need relief; Islam came to grant that relief, contrary to the assumption that humans are strong.
ELMALILI:4:28/r5.anchor: İnsanlar zannettikleri gibi kavî bir mahluk değildirler. Şiddete dayanamazlar, tahfîfe muhtaçtırlar ve dîn-i İslâm onlara bu tahfîfi bahşetmek için gelmiştir.

ELMALILI:4:28/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:28/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:28/r6.claim: Marriage rules and dealings should be made easier, avoiding undue restrictions that could open the way to fornication or misuse.
ELMALILI:4:28/r6.anchor: nikâh hususunda da teşdîdât gösterilmemeli, zinâya ve sû’-i isti‘mâle meydan vermemek için ahkâm ve mu‘âmelât-ı nikâh teshil olunmalıdır.

ELMALILI:4:28/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:28/r7.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:4:28/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says eight verses in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ are better for this community than everything on which the sun rises and sets; Elmalılı lists them.
ELMALILI:4:28/r7.anchor: İbn Abbas hazretlerinden mervîdir ki şöyle demiştir: Sûre-i Nisâ’da sekiz âyet bu ümmet için güneşin üzerine doğduğu ve battığı şeylerin hepsinden hayırlıdır.

ELMALILI:4:28/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:28/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:28/r8.claim: He transitions to the next address because marriage has a particular connection with financial ability and the acquisition and management of wealth.
ELMALILI:4:28/r8.anchor: nikâhın kudret-i mâliye ile bir alâka-i mahsûsası bulunmasına mebnî emvâlin kesb ü tasarrufuna müte‘allik

QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r1.claim: God lightens sins through repeated litanies whose lights enter the heart.
QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r1.anchor: يعني ثقل الأوزار بمواترة الأوراد إلى قلوبكم

QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r2.claim: God lightens spiritual struggle through lights of witnessing entering the heart.
QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r2.anchor: ويقال يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم مقاساة المجاهدات بما يلج لقلوبكم من أنوار المشاهدات

QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r3.claim: God lightens the toil of service through the sweetness of obedience.
QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r3.anchor: يخفف عنكم أتعاب الخدمة بحلاوة الطاعات

QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r4.claim: God lightens the burden of trust by carrying it for people.
QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r4.anchor: ويقال يخفف عنكم كلف الأمانة بحملها عنكم

QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r5.claim: Human weakness describes people's poverty and need, which serves as an excuse for them.
QUSHAYRI:v1p203/r5.anchor: { وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا } : وصف بهذا فقرهم وضرهم

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r1.claim: Human weakness does not mean lacking the strength and equipment to pass the test of servitude; it means having vulnerabilities alongside will and power as part of the test.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r1.anchor: İnsanın zayıf yaratılmasından maksat, kulluk imtihanını kazanabilecek kadar güç ve donanımdan mahrum olması değil, imtihan gereği –iradesi ve gücü yanında– bazı zaaflarının bulunmasıdır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r2.claim: Sexual desire is one human weakness; Islam does not erase it with rigid prohibitions but directs people to satisfy it through lawful means.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r2.anchor: Bunlardan biri de cinsel arzudur. İslâm dini, bu tür arzuları yok sayan katı bir yasaklar sistemi getirmeyip bunların meşrû yollardan tatminini istemiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r3.claim: Love of wealth is another weakness; Islam warns about the moral corruption it can cause while encouraging lawful ways of earning.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r3.anchor: insanın zaaflarından biri de mal tutkusudur. İslâm bunun ortaya çıkaracağı ahlâkî bozulmayla ilgili uyarılarda bulunmakla beraber meşrû kazanma yollarını da teşvik etmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r4.claim: God intends ease rather than hardship for His servants, as also stated in 2:185.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r4.anchor: Allah kulları için güçlük değil, kolaylık murat eder (Bakara 2/185)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r5.claim: God does not force people into impossible situations or burdens beyond their capacity; every obligation has concessions that ease it in ordinary or exceptional circumstances.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:28/r5.anchor: onları imtihan için bile olsa çıkmaz yollara zorlamaz, taşınamaz yüklerin altına sokmaz. Her bir yükümlülüğün, olağan üstü veya olağan dışı hallere bağlı kolaylıkları, yükü hafifletici ruhsatları vardır.

BURHAN:v4p223/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p223/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p223/r1.claim: An with its clause can occupy the accusative object position, as in ‘God intends to lighten [the burden] for you.’

SULAMI:v1p144#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p144#3/r1.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p144#3/r1.claim: One gloss says God prescribes servanthood with knowledge of people's weakness and ignorance.
SULAMI:v1p144#3/r1.anchor: قيل : يعني يقال العبودية لعلمه بضعفكم وجهلكم

SULAMI:v1p144#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p144#3/r2.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p144#3/r2.claim: Another says God intends to lighten the immense trust people burdened themselves with through ignorance.
SULAMI:v1p144#3/r2.anchor: وقيل : يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم ما حملتموه بجهلكم

SULAMI:v1p144#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p144#3/r3.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p144#3/r3.claim: A person is weak in judgment and reason, except when God gives the light of certainty; strength comes through certainty, not from the self.
SULAMI:v1p144#3/r3.anchor: قيل : ضعيف الرأي ضعيف العقل إلا من أمره الله بنور اليقين

DAMGHANI:v1p157/r15.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p157/r15.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p157/r15.claim: Takhfīf means making something easier or gentler for you.
DAMGHANI:v1p157/r15.anchor: الثالث : التخفيف التيسير قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r1.claim: Ḍaʿīf derives from ḍaʿf, weakness, the opposite of strength.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r1.anchor: الضعيف : اسم مأخوذ من الضعف : والضعف ضد القوة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r2.claim: The noun has two vocalizations: ḍaʿf with fatḥa on ḍād or ḍuʿf with ḍamma.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r2.anchor: وفيه لغتان ضعف وضعف بفتح الضاد وضمها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r3.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الضعيف في القرآن على سبعة أوجه : أحدها : العاجز

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r4.claim: Here ḍaʿīf means having little patience.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الضعيف في القرآن على سبعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الضعيف في القرآن على سبعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r6.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الضعيف في القرآن على سبعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r7.claim: Ḍaʿīf means one who is oppressed in 28:5.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r7.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الضعيف في القرآن على سبعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r8.claim: Ḍuʿafāʾ refers to the lowly or socially inferior in 34:31.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r8.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الضعيف في القرآن على سبعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p405/r9.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الضعيف في القرآن على سبعة أوجه

MAJAZ:v1p123/r11.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p123/r11.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p123/r11.claim: Lā taqtulū anfusakum means do not destroy yourselves.
MAJAZ:v1p123/r11.anchor: «ولا تقتلوا أنفسكم» (28) أي لا تهلكوها. «ولكل جعلنا موالي» (32)

NAHHAS:v1p447/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p447/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p447/r10.claim: Khuliqa is passive, and ḍaʿīfan is a circumstantial accusative.
NAHHAS:v1p447/r10.anchor: ( وخلق الإنسان ) اسم ما لم يسم فاعله

NAHHAS:v1p447/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p447/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p447/r11.claim: Desire, appetite, and anger easily sway people; this weakness makes divine concessions necessary.
NAHHAS:v1p447/r11.anchor: ومعناه أن هواه يستميله وشهوته وغضبه يستخفانه وهذا أشد الضعف

SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r1.claim: Yurīdu Allāhu an yukhaffifa is most likely an independent sentence; alternatively it is circumstantial under the earlier yurīdu in “God wants to turn to you.”
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r1.anchor: في هذه الجملة احتمالان أحدهما: وهو الأصح أنها مستأنفة لا محل لها من الإعراب

SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r2.claim: The circumstantial parse separates the clause from its governor with an unrelated coordinated sentence, and links through an overt noun where a circumstantial clause normally needs a pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r2.anchor: وفي هذا الإعراب نظر من وجهين، أحدهما: أنه يؤدي إلى الفصل بين الحال وبين عاملها بجملة معطوفة على جملة العامل في الحال

SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r3.claim: The omitted object of “lighten” is variously supplied as the burden of reasoning and dispelling confusion, or the sin of what people commit.
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r3.anchor: ولم يذكر مفعول التخفيف فهو محذوف فقيل: تقديره: يخفف عنكم تكليف النظر وإزالة الحيرة

SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r4.claim: The clearest analysis of ḍaʿīfan is an emphatic circumstantial accusative describing al-insān.
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r4.anchor: قوله: " ضعيفا " في نصبه أربعة أوجه، الأظهر: أنه حال من " الإنسان " وهي حال مؤكدة

SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r5.claim: The proposed tamyīz analysis is faulty even though the word could accept min before it.
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r5.anchor: الثاني: أنه تمييز قالوا: لأنه يصلح لدخول " من " وهذا غلط

SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r6.claim: Another parse deletes the preposition and qualified noun: God created the human from a weak substance, such as lowly water or a drop.
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r6.anchor: الأصل: خلق من شيء ضعيف أي: من ماء مهين أو من نطفة

SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya treats ḍaʿīfan as a second object by taking khalaqa as jaʿala; al-Samīn calls this unusual because jaʿala meaning “create” takes one object.
SAMIN-DURR:4:28/r7.anchor: والرابع: وإليه أشار ابن عطية أنه منصوب على أنه مفعول ثان

ZAJJAJ:v2p43/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p43/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p43/r4.claim: Human beings are weak because desire draws and sways them.

ASAD-NOTES:4:28#n37/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:28#n37/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:28#n37/r1.claim: God lightens the human burden through guidance that reconciles spiritual and bodily impulses and brings both elements of human nature to full fruition.
ASAD-NOTES:4:28#n37/r1.anchor: to remove, by means of His guidance, all possibility of conflict between man's spirit and his bodily urges

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p154/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p154/r1.speaker: طاوس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p154/r1.claim: Ṭāwūs explains human weakness as weakness in relation to women.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p154/r1.anchor: عن ابن طاوس عن أبيه في قوله تعالى ﴿ وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا ﴾ قال في أمر النساء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p154/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p154/r2.speaker: سلمة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p154/r2.claim: Salama clarifies the weakness as the man’s being weakest at the moment of intercourse.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p154/r2.anchor: قال يريد عند الوطء إنه أضعف ما يكون الرجل بعد أليس كذلك قال سلمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r1.claim: Mujāhid, Ṭāwūs, and Ibn Zayd take human weakness here specifically as weakness regarding women, for which God eased the rules by permitting enslaved women.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد وطاووس وابن زيد: الإخبار عن ضعف الإنسان إنما هو في باب النساء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r2.speaker: طاووس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r2.claim: Ṭāwūs says a person is never weaker than in matters involving women.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r2.anchor: قال طاووس: ليس يكون الإنسان أضعف منه في أمر النساء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r3.speaker: ابن المسيب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r3.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib says Satan never gives up on Adam's descendants without approaching them through women; at eighty, with one eye gone, he still desired with the other and feared women's temptation most.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r3.anchor: وقال ابن المسيب: ما أيس الشيطان من بني آدم قط إلا أتاهم من النساء، فقد أتى علي ثمانون سنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains weakness as inability to resist desires and to bear the burdens of worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r4.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ضعيفا لا يصبر عن الشهوات، وعلى مشاق الطاعات.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says that after the immediate easing through permission of enslaved women, the verse expresses God's broader favor: all the ways He eases religion and makes it manageable.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ثم بعد هذا المقصد أي: تخفيف الله بإباحة الإماء، يخرج الآية مخرج التفضل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r6.speaker: الراغب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r6.claim: Al-Rāghib says weakness is relative to the higher celestial realm, to the human being considered apart from divine aid, or to human need and dependence on one another.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r6.anchor: قال الراغب: ووصف الإنسان بأنه خلق ضعيفا، إنما هو باعتباره بالملأ الأعلى نحو: أأنتم أشد خلقا أم السماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r7.speaker: الراغب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r7.claim: Al-Rāghib also relates weakness to humanity's beginning and end, but says intellect and the capacity for vicegerency and nearness to God in the afterlife make humans strongest in this world.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r7.anchor: أو اعتبارا بمبدئه ومنتهاه كما قال تعالى: الله الذي خلقكم من ضعف فأما إذا اعتبر بعقله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r8.speaker: الراغب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r8.claim: Al-Rāghib contrasts human weakness with God's favoring people over many created beings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r8.anchor: ولهذا قال تعالى: وفضلناهم على كثير ممن خلقنا تفضيلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r9.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains weakness by humanity's creation from despised fluid and links it to the statement that God created people from weakness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن: ضعيفا لأنه خلق من ماء مهين. قال الله تعالى: الذي خلقكم من ضعف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid read the verb in the active voice, with God's name understood as its subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ومجاهد: وخلق الإنسان مبنيا للفاعل مسندا إلى ضمير اسم الله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r11.claim: On the active reading ضعيفا is a circumstantial accusative; parsing it as specification is rejected because a من phrase could be supplied.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r11.anchor: وانتصاب ضعيفا على الحال. وقيل: انتصب على التمييز. لأنه يجوز أن يقدر بمن،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r12.claim: Another parse deletes a preposition and adjective: the sense is created from something weak, such as clay or the stages of embryonic development.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r12.anchor: وقيل: انتصب على إسقاط حرف الجر، والتقدير: من شيء ضعيف، أي من طين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r13.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says خلق can mean جعل and make ضعيفا a second object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r13.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويصح أن يكون خلق بمعنى جعل، فيكسبها ذلك قوة التعدي إلى مفعولين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r14.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says no grammarian makes خلق transitive to two objects by interpreting it as جعل; rather, جعل meaning خلق takes one object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p604/r14.anchor: وهذا هو الذي ذكره من أن خلق يتعدى إلى اثنين بجعلها بمعنى جعل، لا أعلم أحدا من النحويين

ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r1.speaker: طاوس ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r1.claim: Tawus and Mujahid say God lightens the rules about women and marriage by permitting marriage to enslaved women; al-Alusi's later contextual argument supports this reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r1.anchor: أي في التكليف في أمر النساء والنكاح بإباحة نكاح الإماء قاله طاوس ومجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r2.claim: Another view takes the easing generally: God lightened obligations for this community compared with earlier communities.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r2.anchor: وقيل : يخفف في التكليف على العموم فإنه تعالى خفف عن هذه الأمة ما لم يخفف عن غيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r3.claim: A further view says God eases matters by accepting repentance and enabling people to repent.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r3.anchor: وقيل : يخفف بقبول التوبة والتوفيق لها

ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r4.claim: The sentence is independent and has no grammatical position in what precedes.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r4.anchor: والجملة مستأنفة لا محل لها من الإعراب

ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r5.speaker: طاوس
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r5.claim: Tawus says human weakness here concerns women: a man cannot patiently abstain from them.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r5.anchor: أي في أمر النساء لا يصبر عنهن قاله طاوس

ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r6.claim: An unnamed report says there is no good in women and no patience without them: they overcome a noble man, while a noble man does not overcome them, and the speaker prefers being nobly overcome.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r6.anchor: وفي الخبر لا خير في النساء ولا صبر عنهن يغلبن كريما ويغلبهن لئيم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r7.claim: Other explanations say desire sways a person, fear and grief unsettle him, or he cannot oppose appetite and bear the hardship of obedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r7.anchor: وقيل : يستميله هواه وشهوته ويستشيطه خوفه وحزنه وقيل : عاجز عن مخالفة الهوى وتحمل مشاق الطاعة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r8.claim: Another view calls people weak in judgment: only divine light lets them discern hidden secrets and wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r8.anchor: وقيل : ضعيف الرأي لا يدرك الأسرار والحكم إلا بنور إلهي

ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r9.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says the weakness is physical: even a small event causes pain; al-Alusi rejects this and weak judgment as poorly supported by the context, which concerns the marriage dispensation.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r9.anchor: وعن الحسن رضي الله تعالى عنه أن المراد ضعيف الخلقة يؤلمه أدنى حادث نزل به

ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r10.claim: Weak is parsed as an accusative circumstantial, or as if a preposition meaning from had been omitted before weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r10.anchor: ونصب ضعيفا على الحال وقيل : على نزع الخافض أي من ضعيف

ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r11.claim: The alternative construed as created from a weak substance, whether clay or semen, does not fit the context.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r11.anchor: وأريد به الطين أو النطفة وكلاهما كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the verb actively, with God as its subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r12.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ( وخلق الإنسان ) على البناء للفاعل والضمير لله عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r13.claim: Al-Bayhaqi reports Ibn Abbas saying that eight verses in Surat al-Nisa are better for this community than all that the sun rises and sets upon, listing 4:26, 4:27, 4:28, 4:31, 4:40, 4:110, 4:48, and 4:152.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p14#3/r13.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي في الشعب عنه أنه قال : ثماني آيات نزلت في سورة النساء هي خير لهذه الأمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r1.claim: God intends to make the rules of religious law easier for you; the author links this to the verse about removing burdens.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r1.anchor: يسهل عليكم في أحكام الشرع، وقد سهل كما قال جل ذكره: "ويضع عنهم إصرهم"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r2.claim: The Prophet described his mission as bringing the upright, tolerant, and easy religion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r2.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "بعثت بالحنيفية السمحة السلهة"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r3.speaker: طاووس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r3.claim: Tawus and al-Kalbi explain human weakness in relation to women: a person cannot patiently abstain from them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r3.anchor: قال طاووس والكلبي وغيرهما في أمر النساء: لا يصبر عنهن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r4.speaker: ابن كيسان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kaysan says desire and appetite draw a person toward what is wanted.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: {وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا} يستميله هواه وشهوته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says human weakness refers to being created from lowly fluid, as another verse states.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p199#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو أنه خلق من ماء مهين، بيانه قوله تعالى: "الله الذي خلقكم من ضعف"

BIQAI-FULL:v2p245/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p245/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p245/r5.claim: God lightens their burden by lifting restrictions imposed on earlier peoples and granting concessions, including marriage to a slave woman as discussed earlier.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p245/r5.anchor: فيضع عنكم الآصار التي كانت على من كان قبلكم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p245/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p245/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p245/r6.claim: The coordinating waw gives the reason for the lightening: human beings were created weak, so burdensome rules are difficult for them.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p245/r6.anchor: لأنكم خلقتم ضعفاء يشق عليكم الثقل

BIQAI-FULL:v2p245/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p245/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p245/r7.claim: Human weakness consists in need: people cannot abstain from marriage and other appetites or act without God's support.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p245/r7.anchor: لا يصبر عن النكاح ولا غيره من الشهوات

BIQAI-FULL:v2p245/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p245/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p245/r8.claim: The passage moves from earlier treatment of wealth in inheritance and marriage to rules for handling money; human weakness disproves the claim that women and minors should lose inheritance, while financial rules protect lineage.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p245/r8.anchor: فبطل تعليلهم لمنع النساء والصغار من الإرث بالضعف

DURR-FULL:v2p491/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p491/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p491/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas says eight verses in al-Nisa are better for this community than all sunrise and sunset; the excerpt names 4:26, 4:27, 4:28, and 4:31 among them.
DURR-FULL:v2p491/r14.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: ثماني آيات نزلت في سورة النساء

IBNABIHATIM:v3p926/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p926/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v3p926/r1.claim: Mujāhid says God's easing includes marriage to slave women and everything in which there is ease.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p926/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : يريد الله ان يخفف عنكم يقول : في نكاح الامة وفي كل شيء فيه يسر .

IBNABIHATIM:v3p926/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p926/r2.speaker: طاوس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p926/r2.claim: Ṭāwūs explains human weakness as weakness regarding women: a person cannot restrain himself from them.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p926/r2.anchor: عن ابن طاوس ، عن أبيه وخلق الانسان ضعيفا قال : في شان النساء ، اي : لا يصبر عنهن .

IBNABIHATIM:v3p926/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p926/r3.speaker: وكيع
IBNABIHATIM:v3p926/r3.claim: Wakīʿ elaborates that a man's reason leaves him when he is around women.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r1.claim: Following the explanation in 4:26, this verse reminds the community that God continues to intend ease and care for it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r1.anchor: بالتذكير بأن الله لا يزال مراعيا رفقه بهذه الأمة وإرادته بها اليسر دون العسر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r2.claim: The law balances securing benefits and averting harms gently; it can waive some harms when avoiding them would impose hardship or block a benefit, as with permission for those unable to afford free women to marry enslaved women.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r2.anchor: فربما ألغت الشريعة بعض المفاسد إذا كان في الحمل على تركها مشقة أو تعطيل مصلحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r3.claim: The principle of ease is reinforced by verses denying hardship, preferring ease, and lifting burdens from earlier communities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r3.anchor: والآيات الدالة على هذا المعنى بلغت مبلغ القطع كقوله : { وما جعل عليكم في الدين من حرج }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r4.claim: A hadith the author calls authentic says this religion is easy and whoever makes it burdensome will be overcome by it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r4.anchor: في الحديث الصحيح : ( إن هذا الدين يسر ولن يشاد هذا الدين أحد إلا غلبه )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r5.claim: The Prophet instructed Muʿadh and Abu Musa to make matters easy and not difficult.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r5.anchor: فقال لمعاذ وأبي موسى : ( يسرا ولا تعسرا )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r6.claim: The Prophet said that his envoys had been sent as bearers of good news, not as people who repel others.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r6.anchor: وقال : ( إنما بعثتم مبشرين لا منفرين )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r7.claim: When Muʿadh complained about an imam who prolonged prayer, the Prophet rebuked him with “Are you putting people to trial?”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r7.anchor: وقال لمعاذ لما شكا بعض المصلين خلفه من تطويله ( أفتان أنت )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r8.claim: Ease is a foundational principle of Islamic law from which the two kinds of legal concessions branch.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22/r8.anchor: فكان التيسير من أصول الشريعة الإسلامية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22#2/r1.claim: The statement that humanity was created weak is a concluding generalization and a rationale for easing; it presents Islam as especially suited to people in every time and place, unlike earlier religions that addressed particular conditions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22#2/r1.anchor: وإظهار لمزية هذا الدين وأنه أليق الأديان بالناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22#2/r2.claim: The wording is linked to the declaration that God has now lightened the burden because He knows the believers are weak.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22#2/r2.anchor: ومن هذا المعنى قوله تعالى : { الآن خفف الله عنكم وعلم أن فيكم ضعفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22#2/r3.speaker: طاووس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22#2/r3.claim: Tawus says a person is weaker in no matter than in the matter of women; Ibn ʿAshur says this is included but does not exhaust the verse’s meaning, since some rulings eased marriage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p22#2/r3.anchor: قال طاووس ليس يكون الإنسان في شيء أضعف منه في أمر النساء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r3.claim: Taḍmin is a form of ellipsis in which a verb or adjective carries the sense of another, indicated by a dependent such as a preposition, so the sentence conveys two meanings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r3.anchor: والتضمين أن يضمن الفعل أو الوصف معنى فعل أو وصف آخر ويشار إلى المعنى المضمن بذكر ما هو من متعلقاته من حرف أو معمول فيحصل في الجملة معنيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r4.claim: Qur'anic proverbial expressions are unusually effective in Arabic; Ibn Ashur says the Qur'an surpasses the literary achievement that made Zuhayr's poem a Muallaqa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r4.anchor: ومن هذا الباب ما اشتمل عليه من الجمل الجارية مجرى الأمثال ، وهذا باب من أبواب البلاغة نادر في كلام بلغاء العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r5.claim: Expansive description is used to instill fear; Ibn Ziyaba's verse about Amr hiding his head while threatening his maternal uncles illustrates the Arabic pattern.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r5.anchor: كقول ابن زيابة : نبئت عمرا غارزا رأسه في سنة يوعد أخواله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r6.claim: The Qur'an can intend multiple senses of a polysemous word, including literal and figurative meanings when context allows, increasing meaning concisely as part of its inimitability.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r6.anchor: ومن أساليب القرآن المنفرد بها التي أغفل المفسرون اعتبارها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r8.claim: The literary registers of forcefulness and gentleness each suit their context and reach their height in the Qur'an; this verse exemplifies gentleness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r8.anchor: فبينما تسمعه يقول ) قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا إنه هو الغفور الرحيم ( ويقول ) يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r9.claim: A forceful warning exemplifies the Qur'an's contrasting register of majesty alongside gentleness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p122/r9.anchor: إذ تسمعه يقول ) فإن أعرضوا فقل أنذرتكم صاعقة مثل صاعقة عاد وثمود (

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r1.claim: The verse's apparent immediate point is God's easing the burden of marriage by permitting marriage to enslaved women, because people struggle to restrain desire for women.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r1.anchor: المقصد الظاهر بهذه الآية أنها في تخفيف الله تعالى ترك نكاح الإماء بإباحة ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد وطاوس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r2.claim: Mujahid, Ibn Zayd, and Tawus likewise understand human weakness here as weakness in resisting sexual desire for women.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r2.anchor: وكذلك قال مجاهد وابن زيد وطاوس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r3.speaker: طاوس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r3.claim: Tawus says people are weaker in no matter than in matters concerning women.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r3.anchor: وقال طاوس: ليس يكون الإنسان في شيء أضعف منه في أمر النساء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r4.claim: Beyond the immediate case, the verse expresses God's gracious easing in all matters and the ease of religion; human weakness is general because desire usually tempts people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r4.anchor: ثم بعد هذا المقصد تخرج الآية في مخرج التفضل، لأنها تتناول كل ما خفف الله تعالى عن عباده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r5.claim: In the majority reading, al-insan is passive-voice subject and da'ifan is a circumstantial accusative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r5.anchor: والإنسان رفع على ما لم يسم فاعله، وضعيفا حال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid read the verb actively, with da'ifan still a circumstantial accusative; khalaqa may mean ja'ala, making it transitive to two objects and da'ifan the second.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p40#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ومجاهد «وخلق الإنسان» على بناء الفعل للفاعل وضعيفا حال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r1.claim: Takhfīf means making a legal duty easier or removing part of it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r1.anchor: التخفيف تسهيل التكليف أو إزالة بعضه قال ابن جرير والمعنى يريد أن ييسر لكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r2.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r2.claim: Ibn Jarir says the easing is permission to marry believing slave women when one cannot afford a free woman.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r2.anchor: قال ابن جرير والمعنى يريد أن ييسر لكم باذنه في نكاح الفتيات المؤمنات لمن لم يستطع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r3.claim: One view says human weakness is innate: people were created from lowly fluid.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r3.anchor: أحدها أنه الضعف في أصل الخلقة قال الحسن هو أنه خلق من ماء مهين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r4.speaker: طاووس، مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r4.claim: A second view says human weakness is limited patience in resisting women.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r4.anchor: والثاني أنه قلة الصبر عن النساء قاله طاووس ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r5.speaker: الزجاج، ابن كيسان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r5.claim: A third view says human weakness is a lack of resolve to master desire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p60/r5.anchor: والثالث أنه ضعف العزم عن قهر الهوى وهذا قول الزجاج وابن كيسان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r4.claim: God intends to make His laws, commands, prohibitions, and decreed circumstances lighter for people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r4.anchor: أي: في شرائعه وأوامره ونواهيه وما يقدره لكم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r5.claim: Mujahid and others cite the conditional permission to marry enslaved women as an example of God’s legal easing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r5.anchor: ولهذا أباح [نكاح] (6) الإماء بشروطه، كما قال مجاهد وغيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r6.claim: Human weakness of nature, resolve, and aspiration makes divine legal easing appropriate.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r6.anchor: {خلق الإنسان ضعيفا} فناسبه (7) التخفيف؛ لضعفه في نفسه وضعف عزمه وهمته.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r7.speaker: ابن طاوس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r7.claim: Ibn Tawus transmits from his father that human weakness here concerns women; Waki explains that a man’s reason leaves him around them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r7.anchor: عن ابن طاوس، عن أبيه: {خلق الإنسان ضعيفا} أي: في أمر النساء، وقال وكيع: يذهب عقله عندهن.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r8.speaker: موسى الكليم عليه الصلاة والسلام
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r8.claim: On the Miʿraj return, Moses urges Muhammad to request relief from fifty daily prayers, saying earlier peoples failed at fewer; Muhammad repeatedly returns until five remain, made equivalent to fifty by tenfold reward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p267/r8.anchor: وقال موسى الكليم عليه الصلاة والسلام (9) لنبينا صلوات الله وسلامه (10) عليه ليلة الإسراء حين مر عليه راجعا من عند سدرة المنتهى،

JISHUMI:v2p1525/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1525/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1525/r2.claim: Takhfīf means making something easier; easing a burden is like reducing its weight.
JISHUMI:v2p1525/r2.anchor: والتخفيف: التسهيل، والخفة خلاف الثقل، والتخفيف على النفس بالتيسير كتخفيف الحمل بخفة الوزن

JISHUMI:v2p1525/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1525/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1525/r3.claim: Weakness is the opposite of strength.

JISHUMI:v2p1525/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1525/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1525/r4.claim: Heaviness and strength are positive qualities, while lightness and weakness are absences of heaviness and strength rather than independent qualities.
JISHUMI:v2p1525/r4.anchor: والخفة ليست بمعنى، والثقل معنى؛ وهو الاعتماد اللازم شغلا، والقوة معنى، والضعف ليس بمعنى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533/r7.claim: God lightens the burden by permitting marriage to enslaved women and granting other legal concessions.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533/r7.anchor: بإحلال نكاح الأمة وغيره من الرخص

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533#2/r1.claim: Human beings are weak: they cannot patiently resist desires or bear the hardships of acts of obedience.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533#2/r1.anchor: لا يصبر عن الشهوات وعلى مشاق الطاعات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533#2/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib says Satan never despairs of Adam’s descendants, but approaches them through women; at eighty, despite failing eyesight, he still feared that temptation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533#2/r2.anchor: وعن سعيد بن المسيب ما أيس الشيطان من بني آدم قط الا اتاهم من قبل النساء فقد اتى علي ثمانون سنة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads the verb in the active voice, with al-insān accusative.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ( وخلق الإنسان ) على البناء للفاعل ونصب الإنسان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says eight passages in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ are better for this community than sunrise and sunset; the first three are the verses on clarification, repentance, and relief.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p533#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ( وخلق الإنسان ) على البناء للفاعل ونصب الإنسان وعنه رضي الله عنه ثمان آيات في سورة النساء هي خير لهذه الأمة مما طلعت عليه الشمس وغربت

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p473/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p473/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p473/r4.claim: God's easing concerns marrying enslaved women.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p473/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p473/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p473/r5.claim: Human beings are weak in their ability to endure abstinence from intercourse with women.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p473/r5.anchor: وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا عن احتمال الصبر عن جماع النساء

MUJAHID:v1p153#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p153#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p153#2/r1.claim: God's easing includes marriage to enslaved women and every matter in which He grants a concession.
MUJAHID:v1p153#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم ﴾ يعني في نكاح الإماء وفي كل شيء رخص فيه

MUQATIL:4:26-28/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:26-28/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:26-28/r3.claim: God lightens the burden by allowing a man who cannot afford a free wife to marry a slave woman, so he does not fornicate.
MUQATIL:4:26-28/r3.anchor: إذ رخص فى تزويج الأمة لمن لم يجد طولا لحرة

MUQATIL:4:26-28/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:26-28/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:26-28/r4.claim: Humans are weak because they cannot patiently refrain from marriage; hence God permits marriage to slave women to prevent fornication.
MUQATIL:4:26-28/r4.anchor: لا يصبر عن النكاح، ويضعف عن تركه، فلذلك أحل لهم تزويج الولائد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p218/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p218/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p218/r1.claim: God eases matters by permitting marriage to enslaved women and granting other legal dispensations.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p218/r1.anchor: باحلال نكاح الأمة وغيره من الرخص

NASAFI-FULL:v1p218/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p218/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p218/r2.claim: Human beings are weak: they cannot patiently resist desires or endure the hardships of worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p218/r2.anchor: لا يصبر عن الشهوات وعلى مشاق الطاعات

BURSEVI:v2p153#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p153#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p153#2/r11.claim: God lightens the burdens of duty by prescribing a tolerant, easy religious law and granting concessions in difficult circumstances, including marriage to bondwomen.
BURSEVI:v2p153#2/r11.anchor: ما في عهدتكم من مشاق التكاليف فلذلك شرع لكم الشرعة الحنيفية السمحة السهلة

BURSEVI:v2p153#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p153#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p153#2/r12.claim: Human beings are weak because they cannot reliably resist their appetites and powers, endure desires, or wield their strength through difficult acts of obedience.
BURSEVI:v2p153#2/r12.anchor: عاجزا عن مخالفة هواه غير قادر على مقابلة دواعيه وقواه

BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r5.claim: Human weakness means a person cannot endure separation from God for even a moment; humans are praised for this weakness because they are specially marked by mutual love of God.
BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r5.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الإنسان لا يصبر عن الله لحظة لضعفه مهما يكون على الفطرة الإنسانية فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها فإنه يحبهم ويحبونه

BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r6.claim: Weakness is both a cause of human perfection and happiness and a cause of deficiency and misery: people shift between animal appetites and angelic praise and obedience.
BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r6.anchor: هذا الضعف سبب لكمال الإنسان وسعادته وسبب لنقصانه وشقاوته لأنه يتغير لضعفه من حال إلى حال ومن صفة إلى أخرى

BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r7.claim: Only humans possess this capacity to move between animal and angelic qualities; weakness lets them perfect themselves by adopting God's attributes, unlike angels or beasts.
BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r7.anchor: وليس هذا الاستعداد لغيره حتى الملك لا يقدر أن يتصف بصفات البهيمة والبهيمة لا تقدر أن تتصف بصفة الملك لعدم ضعف الإنسانية

BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r8.speaker: الله تعالى
BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r8.claim: A divine hadith promises that whoever obeys God will be made a living king who never dies, illustrating human perfection through obedience.
BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r8.anchor: أنا ملك حي لا أموت أبدا عبدي أطعني أجعلك ملكا حيا لا يموت أبدا

BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r9.claim: At perfection a human is the best of creation, while adopting beastly qualities makes him the worst of creation.
BURSEVI:v2p154#2/r9.anchor: فعند هذا الكمال يكون خير البرية وعند اتصافه بالصفات البهيمية يصير شر البرية

QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r2.claim: أن يخفف is likewise an accusative complement governed by يريد.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r2.anchor: وكذلك { يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم } ف { أن يخفف } في موضع نصب ب { يريد }

QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r4.claim: The preferred interpretation is that God’s lightening encompasses all the rulings of the sacred law.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r4.anchor: قيل: هذا في جميع أحكام الشرع، وهو الصحيح.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r5.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد وطاوس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r5.claim: Mujāhid, Ibn Zayd, and Ṭāwūs restrict the lightening to permitting slave marriage because people are weak before sexual desire.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r5.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالتخفيف نكاح الأمة، أي لما علمنا ضعفكم عن الصبر عن النساء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r6.speaker: طاوس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r6.claim: Ṭāwūs says a person is weaker in no matter than in relation to women.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r6.anchor: قال طاوس: ليس يكون الإنسان في شيء أضعف منه في أمر النساء.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r12.claim: The phrase “the human was created weak” is in the accusative as a circumstantial expression.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r12.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا } نصب على الحال

QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r13.claim: Human desire, passion, and anger readily sway a person; this severe weakness makes legal easing necessary.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r13.anchor: والمعنى أن هواه يستميله وشهوته وغضبه يستخفانه، وهذا أشد الضعف فاحتاج إلى التخفيف.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r14.speaker: طاوس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r14.claim: Ṭāwūs limits the human weakness in this phrase to weakness concerning women.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r14.anchor: وقال طاوس: ذلك في أمر النساء خاصة.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to read the phrase as “God created the human weak,” explaining weakness as inability to be patient with women.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r15.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قرأ { وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا } أي وخلق الله الإنسان ضعيفا، أي لا يصبر عن النساء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r16.speaker: ابن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r16.claim: Ibn al-Musayyab says that even at eighty, with severe sensory decline, he still feared the temptation of women.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r16.anchor: قال ابن المسيب: لقد أتى علي ثمانون سنة وذهبت إحدى عيني وأنا أعشو بالأخرى وصاحبي أعمى أصم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r17.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r17.claim: ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit describes his frailty yet says he would not be alone with an unlawful woman even for the world, fearing Satan’s temptation; Yaḥyā glosses his bodily expressions.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:27-28/r17.anchor: ونحوه عن عبادة بن الصامت رضي الله عنه، قال عبادة: ألا تروني لا أقوم إلا رفدا ولا آكل إلا ما لوق لي

RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r1.claim: Mujāhid and Muqātil take the easing to mean permission to marry a slave woman when necessary.
RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r1.anchor: الأول : المراد منه إباحة نكاح الأمة عند الضرورة وهو قول مجاهد ومقاتل

RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r2.speaker: الباقون
RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r2.claim: Other commentators read the easing generally: God made all legal duties easier and more gracious than the burdens imposed on the Children of Israel.
RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r2.anchor: والباقون قالوا : هذا عام في كل أحكام الشرع ، وفي جميع ما يسره لنا وسهله علينا ، إحسانا منه الينا

RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r3.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r3.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues that if God created human acts, creating unbelief and then forbidding it—or withholding faith while commanding it—would impose the greatest burden; the verse also rules out obligations beyond capacity.
RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r3.anchor: قال القاضي : هذا يدل على أن فعل العبد غير مخلوق لله تعالى ، إذ لو كان كذلك فالكافرين يخلق فيه الكفر

RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī answers al-Qāḍī by citing the counterarguments from divine knowledge and motivating causes established earlier.
RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r4.anchor: والجواب : أنه معارض بالعلم والداعي ، وأكثر ما ذكرناه

RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r5.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r5.claim: Al-Qāḍī explains human weakness as strong impulses toward pleasure and desire that make resisting them difficult, rather than bodily frailty; the motives, not physical capacity, determine strength in obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r5.anchor: والأقرب أنه يحمل الضعف في هذا الموضع لا على ضعف الخلقة ، بل يحمل على كثرة الدواعي إلى اتباع الشهوة واللذة

RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p55#2/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī approves al-Qāḍī's account but says it defeats his Muʿtazilite position: motives require causes, leading either to regress or to their being from God, which is the correct view.

RAZI-FULL:v10p56/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p56/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v10p56/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says eight verses in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ are better for this community than sunrise and sunset, listing verses 4:26–28, 4:31, 4:40, 4:110, 4:116, and 3:147.
RAZI-FULL:v10p56/r1.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال : ثمان آيات في سورة النساء هي خير لهذه الأمة مما طلعت عليه الشمس وغربت

RAZI-FULL:v10p56/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p56/r2.speaker: محمد الرازي
RAZI-FULL:v10p56/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī prays that God make him worthy of the blessings of these verses through divine grace and mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v10p56/r2.anchor: ويقول محمد الرازي مصنف هذا الكتاب ختم الله له بالحسنى

ALUSI-FULL:v5p35#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p35#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p35#2/r8.claim: God eases the burdens of servanthood at the station of witnessing, or eases the self's burden by opening the delight of worship after initial patience.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p35#2/r8.anchor: أثقال العبودية في مقام المشاهدة أو أثقال النفس بفتح باب الاستلذاذ بالعبادة بعد الصبر عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v5p35#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p35#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p35#2/r9.claim: Humans cannot bear unseen disclosures and the force of witnessing without divine aid, or cannot endure a moment's veil from the beloved or separation from the desired.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p35#2/r9.anchor: عن حمل واردات الغيب وسطوات المشاهدة فلا يستطيع حمل ذلك إلا بتأييد إلهي

ALUSI-FULL:v5p35#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p35#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p35#2/r10.claim: Patience is praiseworthy in every circumstance except patience with God, which is blameworthy because of perfect longing.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p35#2/r10.anchor: والصبر يحمد في المواطن كلها إلا عليك فإنه مذموم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p35#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p35#2/r11.speaker: الشبلي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p35#2/r11.claim: Al-Shibli prayed that there is no rest with God and no escape from Him, and sought refuge through God in God.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p35#2/r11.anchor: وكان الشبلي قدس سره يقول : إلهي لا معك قرار ولا منك فرار
